deep.reconstruction:
This is a printed page (p. 7, signature A4) of the elementary arithmetic textbook bound in the 'HB.Leiste' bundle (presumably Christian Leiste's school textbook on arithmetic and algebra). It is not a Gauss derivation. The only handwriting on this page is one small interlinear insertion above 'Dinge' in §8. The cut-off Latin words in the left margin come from the facing (previous) page of Gauss's notes.

Content of §7 (Section II.1, 'common addition and subtraction'):
(a) Addition is the increase of a quantity by another of the same kind. If A + D = C, then C is the sum of the parts A and D.
(b) Subtraction is the decrease of a quantity by another of the same kind. If C - A = D, then D is the difference or remainder between C and A.
(c) How to carry these out with actual numbers is treated as a postulate. Since A + D = C is equivalent to C - A = D, each operation serves as the check ('Probe') of the other.
(d) Addition and subtraction are binary operations. Because a sum or difference is again a number, they extend to several numbers.

Worked example, using the segment division of AB from §3. The segments are AC = 5, CD = 2, DE = 3, EB = 4.
- AD = AC + CD = 5 + 2 = 7.
- AE = AD + DE = 7 + 3 = 10.
- AB = AE + EB = AC + CD + DE + EB = 14.
- Conversely, AB - BE = 14 - 4 = 10 = AE.
- Then AB - BE - ED = AE - ED = 10 - 3 = 7 = AD.
- Then AB - BE - ED - DC = AD - DC = 7 - 2 = 5 (= AC).
- Finally, AB - BE - ED - DC = AB - (BE + ED + DC): subtracting several terms equals subtracting their sum.

§8 begins the axioms ('Grundsätze'):
1) [Only] things of the same kind can be compared and added together.
2) The parts of a whole, added together, equal the whole (continued on the next page).

The handwritten insertion above 'Dinge' appears to restrict axiom 1 to 'Nur Dinge von einerley Art' ('only things of the same kind').
errors: No mathematical errors: all of the arithmetic (5+2=7, 7+3=10, 10+4=14, 14-4=10, 10-3=7, 7-2=5) is correct.
'Foderungs-Sätze' is a period spelling of 'Forderungssätze', not an error.

results.what: Definitions of addition and subtraction as inverse operations, with each serving as the check of the other.
results.modern_name: Addition/subtraction as inverse operations (a + d = c iff c - a = d)

results.what: Extension of the binary operations to several summands, and a - b - c - d = a - (b + c + d).
results.modern_name: Associativity of addition; subtracting a sum

results.what: Axioms: things of the same kind can be compared and added; the parts together equal the whole.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed elementary textbook page, not a Gauss derivation. The only possible Gauss contribution is a one-word interlinear insertion ('Nur'?) in an axiom; it is of no mathematical significance.

checkable.sympy: simplify((a - b - c - d) - (a - (b + c + d))) == 0
checkable.asserts: Successive subtraction equals subtraction of the sum

checkable.sympy: Eq(solve(Eq(A + D, C), D)[0], C - A)
checkable.asserts: A + D = C is equivalent to D = C - A (each operation is the check of the other)

transcription_corrections: The handwritten insertion above 'Dinge' in §8 is transcribed as 'fiur[?]'. It most likely reads 'Nur', giving 'Nur Dinge von einerley Art ...'.

The cut-off handwritten words in the left margin ('...e a liam', '...o', '...cendum ut', '...significet') are not part of this page. They are bleed from the facing leaf of Gauss's Latin notes: 'elicere aliam', '...=0', 'statuendum'/'faciendum', 'significet'/'significatione'.
The numbers in the printed text use '+' signs typeset as '÷'/'+'-like glyphs; all of them should be read as '+'.
